title: Pupil/gaze behavioral data semantics audit (usability gate for real-data gain/arousal nuisance covariates)
purpose: Determine, from actual NWB file structure and value content (not assumption), whether pupil diameter and (x,y) gaze position are legitimately usable as PRE-EVENT, non-leaky nuisance/gain covariates on this corpus, before any trial-aligned extraction code is written or any covariation-with-neural-state claim is made. Gates omission/jnwb_ext/behavioral_covariates.py.

task1_answers.question: 1. Exact data source
task1_answers.answer: Two DISTINCT acquisition groups, NOT PyNWB's standard PupilTracking/EyeTracking extension objects: acquisition/pupil_1_tracking (1-D, pupil diameter) and acquisition/eye_1_tracking (2-D (n,2), gaze x/y). Both are generic NWB TimeSeries/SpatialSeries objects with a custom naming convention, not a dedicated ophys-eye-tracking NWB extension. Layout is NOT uniform across subjects: C31o and V198o store data/starting_time FLAT directly under the group (acquisition/pupil_1_tracking/data, acquisition/pupil_1_tracking/starting_time); V182o nests one level deeper (acquisition/pupil_1_tracking/pupil_1_diameter_data/{data,starting_time}, acquisition/eye_1_tracking/eye_1_tracking_data/{data,starting_time}) -- confirmed across all 10/10 V182o sessions and all 12/12 C31o+V198o sessions via the metadata probe. This is the same footgun class already documented in the omission-data skill for pupil ('no pupil_diameter group, use acquisition/pupil_1_tracking') and now additionally confirmed for eye_1_tracking specifically.
task1_answers.confidence: CONFIRMED (direct h5py structural read, all 22 files)

task1_answers.question: 2. Timestamps/time base
task1_answers.answer: Fixed-rate representation: a scalar starting_time dataset carrying a 'rate' attribute (Hz) and a 'unit'='seconds' attribute -- NOT an explicit per-sample timestamps array. This is the SAME time-base convention jnwb_ext.analog.py already uses for LFP/MUAe (_rate_and_start helper), and this module reuses that exact helper rather than reimplementing timestamp logic. NOTE: an older archived script (omission/scripts/archive_oneoff/build_suite_10_pupil_behavior_reports.py) reads grp['timestamps'][:] as if an explicit array existed -- that code path does not match the CURRENT file structure (no 'timestamps' dataset was found under pupil_1_tracking or eye_1_tracking in any of the 22 files probed here); flagged as a stale assumption in that archived script, not acted on further per ANALYSIS-ONLY doctrine (it is in scripts/archive_oneoff/, not touched).
task1_answers.confidence: CONFIRMED (direct h5py structural read, all 22 files)

task1_answers.question: 3. Sampling rate -- confirm 1000 Hz per-session
task1_answers.answer: The stored 'rate' TimeSeries attribute reads 1000.0 (or a floating-point-noise variant, e.g. 1000.0000000000002) for BOTH pupil and gaze in all 22/22 sessions -- confirming the prior inventory's file-level claim AT THE ATTRIBUTE LEVEL. HOWEVER: V182o's eye_1_tracking group carries an explicit free-text description overriding this -- 'The position of the eye. Actual sampling rate = 500 Hz (Reported=1kHz)' -- present verbatim in ALL 10/10 V182o sessions (sub-V182o_ses-260629 through -260724). This directly CONTRADICTS the prior inventory's blanket '1000 Hz confirmed, uniform, no subject/session gap found' statement for gaze specifically. C31o/V198o carry no such caveat for either pupil or eye (description text is just 'Reconstructed pupil_1_tracking'/'Reconstructed eye_1_tracking', no rate caveat). Pupil for V182o (description 'Pupil diameter.') also carries no rate caveat -- the 500 Hz note is specific to V182o's GAZE channel, not its pupil channel. This is a genuine, corpus-documented (by the file's own metadata) discrepancy the prior inventory missed because it did not read group description text.
task1_answers.confidence: CONFIRMED for the discrepancy's existence and scope (10/10 V182o sessions, gaze only, via description text read on all 22 files); the underlying acquisition mechanism (duplicated samples vs. true interpolation) is UNDETERMINED -- the observed sample-to-sample repeat fraction for V182o gaze in the 2 value-probed V182o sessions (2.0-2.8%) is far below the ~50% a literal every-other-sample duplication would produce, so simple upsampling-by-repetition is NOT what happened; the actual reconstruction/interpolation method is not recoverable from NWB metadata alone.

task1_answers.question: 4. Synchronization with neural signals
task1_answers.answer: acquisition/pupil_1_tracking, acquisition/eye_1_tracking, and every probe's LFP/MUAe series all carry the IDENTICAL starting_time=0.0 / rate=1000.0 convention (confirmed directly for one session per subject) and the same file-level session_start_time/timestamps_reference_time. This is the standard NWB convention of one shared absolute session clock across all acquisition TimeSeries in a file -- pupil/gaze are on the SAME clock basis jnwb_ext.analog.py already assumes for LFP/MUAe, with no separate offset or drift correction documented or needed beyond what LFP alignment already assumes. No corpus convention for an explicit CROSS-DEVICE drift correction exists anywhere in jnwb/ or omission/jnwb_ext (searched); none was found to be necessary given the shared starting_time=0 basis. Physical (uncorrected) inter-device clock drift over a session cannot be ruled out from metadata alone, but this exposure is identical in kind to what LFP/MUAe alignment already carries and accepts -- not a new risk specific to behavioral signals.
task1_answers.confidence: CONFIRMED for the shared starting_time/rate convention (3 sessions, one per subject, all acquisition series); UNDETERMINED for true physical inter-device drift (no independent ground truth available to check against).

task1_answers.question: 5. Units
task1_answers.answer: NOT physically calibrated in any recoverable sense. The stored 'unit' attribute reads 'unknown' for BOTH pupil and eye in C31o/V198o (12/12 sessions); V182o's pupil carries 'arbitrary units' and V182o's eye carries 'meters'. The 'meters' label is NOT credible at face value: observed gaze value range is approximately -5.0..+5.0 in every probed session (see Q8), and a +/-5 METER gaze excursion from a screen at distance_to_screen~1130 (mm, per the intervals table) is physically impossible for an eye-tracking signal -- so this unit label is not trustworthy either. Pupil is NOT raw diameter: raw diameter cannot be negative, yet the majority of samples are negative in every probed session (56-72% non-positive; see Q8/Q9). Gaze coordinate origin/convention could NOT be confirmed: the intervals table's own x_position/y_position DESIGN columns (the task's stimulus placement, not the continuous recording) are mostly NaN with occasional exactly-0.0 values, suggestive of a screen-center-at-origin convention for the TASK, but no numeric relationship between those design columns and the continuously-recorded eye_1_tracking x/y (already on a different, unknown transformed scale) could be established from the data available. Screen geometry IS present and consistent within a session (distance_to_screen, screen_width/height, screen_res_width/height columns, constant per session, e.g. 1130mm/1000x550mm/1920x1080px for the sampled C31o session) but is not usable to back out gaze units without knowing the eye_1_tracking transform.
task1_answers.confidence: CONFIRMED that the unit attribute is not trustworthy / that raw-diameter and calibrated-meters interpretations are both ruled out by the value distribution (6-session value probe); UNDETERMINED for what the actual transform/unit IS, and UNDETERMINED for the gaze coordinate origin convention.

task1_answers.question: 6. Preprocessing already applied upstream vs. raw
task1_answers.answer: Some preprocessing has DEFINITELY already been applied -- the group description for C31o/V198o's pupil_1_tracking and eye_1_tracking literally reads 'Reconstructed pupil_1_tracking'/'Reconstructed eye_1_tracking' (all 12/12 sessions). V182o's descriptions do not use the word 'Reconstructed' but the value range/negative-pupil-mean pattern is consistent across all 3 subjects (see Q8), suggesting a similar transform was applied corpus-wide even where not labeled 'Reconstructed'. The SPECIFIC preprocessing steps (filtering, blink interpolation, normalization formula) are NOT documented anywhere in the NWB metadata, jnwb/, or omission/ that this audit could find.
task1_answers.confidence: CONFIRMED that preprocessing occurred (from the 'Reconstructed' label and the value distribution); UNDETERMINED for the specific algorithm.

task1_answers.question: 7. Missing/invalid-value semantics
task1_answers.answer: NO explicit invalid-sample/blink/track-loss/quality channel exists anywhere in acquisition/ for any of the 6 value-probed sessions (full acquisition key listing confirmed identical structure: eye_1_tracking, photodiode_1_tracking, probe_N_lfp, probe_N_muae, pupil_1_tracking, reward_1_tracking -- no additional validity/likelihood field). Zero NaN samples were found in pupil or gaze across all 6 fully-read sessions (0/18M+ to 0/20M+ samples per session). No large concentration of samples at a fixed sentinel value was found either (pct_at_min, the fraction of samples at the exact observed minimum, is ~1e-7 in every session -- consistent with the tail of a continuous distribution, not a sentinel/fill value). CONCLUSION: this corpus's pupil/gaze channels carry NO distinguishable machine-readable invalid-sample marker of any kind (no NaN, no sentinel, no separate quality channel). Any missingness/blink/track-loss signal, if present at all, is invisible at the per-sample level and can only be inferred statistically (extreme-value proximity, discontinuity jumps) -- this audit's own extraction module documents this as a STATED HEURISTIC, not a ground-truth read.
task1_answers.confidence: CONFIRMED (direct full-array value read, 6/22 sessions, 2 per subject, 0 NaN and no sentinel-value clustering found in any of them).

task1_answers.question: 8. Raw diameter/area vs. transformed/normalized quantity
task1_answers.answer: TRANSFORMED, not raw diameter, area, or any physically-realizable pupil measure. Pupil values range from approximately -5.02 to +3.9 across the 6 probed sessions (session-specific max varies 1.16 to 3.91, min consistently near -5.0x to -5.02x), with 56-72% of samples non-positive and a NEGATIVE mean/median in every session (e.g. sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec: mean=-1.29, median=-1.07, std=1.16). This range/sign pattern is inconsistent with raw diameter (must be positive), inconsistent with a simple z-score (which would have mean~0, not a persistently negative mean varying -0.4 to -1.6 across sessions), and inconsistent with a fixed physical scale. The most that can be said with confidence: it is SOME monotonic (or approximately monotonic) transform of pupil size that has been clipped or naturally bounded near +/-5, applied by an unknown upstream pipeline. Gaze x/y show the same qualitative signature (range approximately -5.0..+5.0, per-session/per-subject-specific mean/std, no NaN).
task1_answers.confidence: CONFIRMED that it is transformed, not raw (from the value distribution, 6-session value probe); UNDETERMINED what the specific transform is.

task1_answers.question: 9. Values during a documented fixation-break/off-screen period
task1_answers.answer: UNDETERMINED. Given the finding in Q7 (no invalid-sample marker exists at all), there is no mechanism to identify, from the continuous pupil/gaze arrays alone, which samples fall during a fixation break or off-screen excursion versus a genuine on-task sample. The intervals table's fixation_window column (per-trial, sparse, mostly NaN with occasional small numeric values like 2.0-25.0 -- units undetermined, plausibly a degrees-of-visual-angle radius) describes the TASK's configured acceptance window, not a measured fixation-adherence signal (same finding already flagged in the prior inventory's row 'fixation state (measured, not task parameter)'). Whether a given continuous sample near a fixation break is meaningful cannot be established from data available to this audit.

task1_answers.question: 10. CRITICAL -- future-sample leakage risk from upstream acquisition/preprocessing
task1_answers.answer: A REAL, DOCUMENTED, UNRESOLVED RISK, not ruled out. The 'Reconstructed' label on C31o/V198o's pupil_1_tracking/eye_1_tracking groups (Q6) is strong circumstantial evidence that SOME gap-filling/interpolation was applied to the raw recording before these NWB files were built. Whether that reconstruction used only past samples (causal) or a centered/acausal window reaching into the future relative to any given sample (e.g. linear interpolation across a blink gap, which by construction uses the sample AFTER the gap) could NOT be determined from NWB metadata -- no processing-module provenance, no filter description, no algorithm name is recorded anywhere accessible to this audit. THIS MEANS: a 'current' sample in this stored signal, especially one near ANY gap the reconstruction filled, may already encode information from a time point later than that sample's own nominal timestamp. This audit does NOT claim leakage is present or absent -- it states the risk is real and unresolved, and that no corpus-level evidence rules it out.
task1_answers.confidence: UNDETERMINED / FLAGGED AS UNRESOLVED RISK -- explicitly not guessed either direction. This is the single most important UNDETERMINED item gating downstream use.

usability_determination.verdict: CONDITIONALLY USABLE as an unnormalized, dataset-specific-scale common-cause PROXY for pre-event gain/arousal state -- NOT as a calibrated physical measurement, and NOT with the future-leakage risk (Q10) fully closed.
rationale: Availability (file presence, 0% session-level gaps, 22/22 sessions, all 3 subjects) is CONFIRMED and matches the prior inventory.

Per-sample validity/missingness CANNOT be read from a ground-truth marker (Q7) -- any QC in downstream code is necessarily a stated statistical heuristic, not a fact about the signal. This is weaker evidentiary footing than, e.g., LFP/MUAe, which carry no comparable ambiguity.

Units/scale are NOT calibrated (Q5, Q8) -- safe for WITHIN-session/WITHIN-subject relative comparison (e.g. z-scoring trials within one session), NOT safe for cross-subject or cross-session comparison of raw magnitude, and NOT interpretable as a physical diameter/mm or degrees-of-visual-angle quantity.

The future-leakage risk from upstream 'Reconstructed' processing (Q10) is real and unresolved. As a structural (not curative) mitigation, the extraction module enforces every window to end at or before the trial's own alignment anchor (hard assertion, hi_ms<=0), mirroring the existing pre-event safety argument used for the amplitude/gain covariate in common_driver_control.py -- this bounds how FAR a leaked future sample could reach (never past the tested event onset) but cannot rule out that a sample WITHIN the pre-event window was itself influenced by a value recorded seconds later, if the upstream reconstruction's smoothing/interpolation window was wide enough to span the pre-event window's own gap structure. This should be read as a caveat carried forward into any downstream scientific claim, not a solved problem.

A corpus-wide subject-specific timing caveat exists for V182o gaze (Q3, 'actual rate 500 Hz') that downstream slope/variability features must account for by treating effective temporal resolution as ~2ms for that subject's gaze channel specifically.
usability_determination.recommendation: Usable for Task 2/3/4 of this effort (extraction + QC + descriptive covariation with independent neural pre-state quantities) WITH the above caveats stated at every use site, exactly as done in behavioral_covariates.py's module docstring. NOT recommended as a drop-in replacement for the existing pre-event LFP-amplitude gain proxy without an explicit, separate validation of whether these caveats materially affect the synthetic gain-confound calibration target (out of scope for this audit per the task's own instruction not to attempt that benchmark here).
